correctness.rationale: All deadlines and both starting parts are described by exact independent geometric waiting-time laws. Greedy first-visit coverage is universally deadline-optimal by count coupling. The reverse-hazard order follows from the geometric probability-generating-function splitting into an independent nonnegative delay and log-concavity of the sum-CDF. The source advantage is at most one step; equality for an unbalanced star K_{a,1} is explicitly handled. Near-balanced limits follow from a fixed-K exponential-summand convergence plus vanishing tail variance, then continuous mapping for independent Gumbels and the logistic difference. The standard-library checker independently passes 4,661 exact-rational assertions and asymptotic-mean diagnostics; finite testing is not a proof of all-order claims.

value.rationale: Optimal selection of an initial source for a deadline-constrained graph exploration is a natural finite-horizon control question. This gives an exact all-parameter source-side answer, an explicit signed finite-mean difference, and the sharp logistic-scale transition between negligible and persistent source preference. Although the total gain is at most one discrete step, the theorem determines the full source-order relation at every deadline and gives a tractable two-bottleneck benchmark. This goes beyond leading-order cover-time or a routine single-collector asymptotic.
